title: Làm ơn nói lại số đó
pronunciation: lahm uhn noy lie soh doh
summary: Different ways to say "Please say the number again" in Vietnam, with the phrase to start with, useful forms, and related next steps.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Làm ơn nói lại số đó answers the traveler question "Please say the number again" in moments when Vietnamese stops making sense. This is for when you think you missed only the number. This is useful for room numbers, gates, fares, and prices. Its job is putting the need first and leaving room for the helper to confirm the detail. The forms below show how tone, setting, or politeness changes the best choice.

sections.body: Listen to each piece, then the whole phrase, so the rhythm feels connected instead of memorized word by word.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Start with Làm ơn nói lại số đó when "Please say the number again" is the main thing you need understood. This is for when you think you missed only the number. It gives the other person room to answer with a confirmation, a handoff, a price, or a follow-up question. If speech still does not land, move to writing, pointing, or showing the exact word on your phone.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: These phrases keep the interaction cooperative when repeating the same words is not helping. For "Please say the number again", the useful move is putting the need first and leaving room for the helper to confirm the detail. Pause after the phrase so the person can confirm before you add more words.

sections.title: Traveler insight
sections.body: In When You Don't Understand, locals often answer with a confirmation, a handoff, a price, or a follow-up question rather than a long explanation. That makes Làm ơn nói lại số đó strongest when you say it once, pause, and let the other person show the next step. If speech still does not land, move to writing, pointing, or showing the exact word on your phone.

sections.body: Keep your tone curious. A sharp tone can make a clarification question sound like a challenge.
